ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Conservation and restoration of statue of Lord Gomateshwara 
*361. SHRI LALIT SURI:  
     DR. VIJAY MALLYA:† 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a), whether it is a fact that the world's tallest statue of Lord Gomateshwara 
and its supporting structures need to156 strengthened, 
† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Dr. Vijay 
Mallya. 

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2005] 
(b) if so, the steps undertaken by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for 
conservation and restoration of the heritage structure; and 
(c) whether there is any proposal with the ASI for installing a lightning conductor 
to protect the statue? 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY): (a) to (c) A 
Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) The monolithic statue of Gomateshwara, carved out of a single 
boulder, is resting firmly on the bedrock. Hence, there is no need for 
strengthening the statue . The cloistered mandapa around the statue is also 
structurally stable. 
The Archaeological Survey of India takes up requisite scientific preservation of 
the statue periodically. An estimate of Rs. 3.39 lakhs has been approved for 
preservation works during the current financial year. There is a proposal to install a 
lightning conductor to protect the Gomateshwara statue during the current year. 
DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Mr. Chairman, Sir, the Government has given an 
extremely precise and to the point reply. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Mr. Mallaya, let the first supplementary be put by Shri 
Lalit Suri. (Interruptions) 
SHRI LALIT SURI: Mr. Chairman, Sir, Lord Gomateshwara, also known 
as Lord Bahubali-a Jain saint, has been worshipped for centuries. Its monolithic 
statue is standing atop one of the hills, Indragiri in Karnataka. It is 56.6 feet tall and is 
the tallest monolithic statue in the world made of granite. It was created in 983 AD 
by Chamundaraya, a general and minister of the Ganga King Rachamatta. It is a 
symbol of peace, tolerance and non-violence. Sir, seeing the importance of this 
great statue, I would like to ask the Minister whether any provision has been made to 
complete the restoration work, including installation of lightning conductors before 
Mahamastak-abhisheka festival, which is going to beheld in 2006, after 12 years. 
SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, the description given by the hon. Member 
is very correct. Mahamastak-abhisheka takes place once in 12 years, is likely to 
attract millions of devotees and pilgrims, in scale, 
2 

[22 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
perhaps, it will only be next to the Kumbh Mela. We are conscious of the 
magnitude of the event. Therefore, this year, the Planning Commission, in 
consultation with the State Government, has sanctioned Rs. 75 crores by way of 
providing infrastructure. I just mention, Sir, .that the monument is made of a 
boulder of granite; it is structurally stable and firm. However, we will go in for 
what may be called hydrophobic treatment so that when the huge and anointing 
ceremony takes place, no damage is caused to the monument. 
DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Mr. Chairman, Sir the hon. Minister has replied 
very, very precisely and has said that the statue of Gomateshwara which is 
carved out of a single boulder is on bedrock and, therefore, safe. Sir, I would like to 
ask a question as to what is the methodology used to determine the safety, not only 
of the statue of Gomateshwara, but also several beautiful historical monuments that 
we have in our country, which, I regret to say, are not cared for in the best of way. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Dr. Mallya, you limit you supplementary to Lord 
Gomateshwara. 
DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Sir, I am limiting it to this particular statue. I would 
like to know from the hon. Minister specifically about the methodology used to 
determine its safety, whether any international experts have actually been consulted. I 
would also like to know whether any preventive maintenance has taken place, or, 
whether we wait for things to happen before we act, particularly keeping in mind 
the Mahamastak-abhisheka that is going to be held in February, 2006, at which 
lakhs of people are expected to attend. 
SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, there are monuments and m onuments. 
This monument is structurally stable. We have our own inhouse expertise. There is 
no report of any kind of possible damage. But, when mahamastaka-abhisheka takes 
place, when millions of people participate, when they offer oblations, certain 
chemical damage could be caused. For that, we are taking preventive measures. I 
have already referred to the method called the hydrophobic treatment. So, we get 
the monument washed properly use a chemical called siliGon-compound so that 
when all kinds of things are offered, the monument is not damaged.

*363. SHRI SURENDRA LATH:† 
     SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:

(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that two Sanskrit Pandits from 
Sikkim were granted Financial Assistance by Government for subsistence till 2003-
04; 
(b) whether for the financial years 2001-02, 2002-03 and 2003-04, a sum 
of Rs. 85,000/- was sanctioned and given to the HRD Department of the 
Government of Sikkim and an amount of Rs. 55,000/-only was paid to the Pandits 
for three years as backlog, if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) whether it is a fact that for the year 2004-05 they have not been paid 
till date and if so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF. HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
1 An amount of Rs. 85000/- was released to Government of Sikkim for 
disbursement as financial assistance to two Sanskrit Pandits for the years 2001-
02, 2002-03 and 2003-04. 
2.Under the Central Plan Scheme for Development of Sanskrit Education, 
financial assistance to Sanskrit Pandits under indigent circumstances was granted 
@ Rs. 10,000/- per annum, after deducting his income from other sources upto the 
year 2002-03. The scheme was revised in 2003-04 and each scholar is to be given 
a maximum of Rs. 24,000/- per annum, without deduction of income from other 
sources. 
3.Government of Sikkim have informed that they have disbursed Rs. 55,500/- 
for the three years to the two Pandits. They have been requested on 5.8.2005 
and again on 20.8.2005 to disburse the remaining amount of Rs. 29,500/- also to 
the two Pandits for the year 2003-04. 
4.Fresh Central Assistance under the scheme for the year 2004.-05 can be 
considered only on receipt of request from the State Government, alongwith utilization 
certificate in respect of grant released earlier Government of Sikkim has not 
submitted these so far.

Listing of Education in Eighth Schedule 
*364. SHRI THANGA TAMIL SELVAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that many States have been demanding shifting of 
'Education' from the Concurrent List to the State List; 
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto; 
(c) whether Government recognise the diverse socio-cultural ethos of this country 
according to which the school curriculum has to be shaped; and 
(d) whether Government would bring a constitutional amendment to shift 
'Education' to the State List? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) No demand has been received from the States for shifting of 
'Education' from the Concurrent List to the State List. 
(c) Government do recognize the diverse social cultural ethos of the country. 
Keeping this in view, the draft National Curriculum Framework for School 
Education (NCFSE), 2005 prepared by the National Council of Educational Research 
and Training (NCERT) which is yet to be finally considered by the Central Advisory Board 
of Education (CABE) reflects these concerns. Its common core will include the history of 
India's freedom movement, the constitutional obligations and other content essential to 
nurture national identity which will cut across subject areas and will be designed to 
promote values such as India's common cultural heritage, egalitarianism democracy and 
secularism, equality of 
7

the sexes, protection of the environment, removal of social barriers, observance fo 
the small family norm and inculcation of the scientific temper. The NCFSE is 
advirosy in nature and is not binding on. the States who can make appropriate 
modifications in their curricula to suite local requirements. 
(d) In view of the replies to parts (a) and (b) above, there is no proposal to 
bring a Constitutional Amendment to shift "Education" to the State list.

[22 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Statement 
(a) The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), New Delhi under the 
Ministry of Home Affairs has informed that at an all India level, 50703 
cases of cruelty by husbanb and his relatives were reported during 2003 
which rose to 55439 during 2004 thereby registering an increase of 9.3% 
in 2004 over 2003. 
(b) As per the Report dated October, 2000 of the National Family Health 
Survey (NFHS-2) 1998-99, the reasons which found acceptance by and 
large among the respondent women for a husband beating his wife 
included: husband suspecting wife of being unfaithful, her natal family not 
giving expected money or other items, wife showing disrespect for in-laws, 
wife going out without telling husband, wife neglecting house or children 
and wife not cooking food properly. 
(c) The Government have taken the following measures to check increase of 
domestic violence against women:— 
 
■ The government has approved for introduction in parliament a legislation 
to protect women from domestic violence. 
■ Setting up of family couselling centres for couseling families in such 
situations. 
■ Setting up of helplines for women in distress. 
■ Support services to victims of violence through schemes such as short 
stay Homes and swadhar under which shelter, maintenance, couseling, 
capacity building, occupational training, medical aid and other 
services are provided. 
■ Redressal of grievances through interventions of National and State 
Commissions for Women. 
■ Organizing legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Camps. 
■ Implementation of schemes for (i) awareness generation and advocacy 
and (ii) economic empowerment of women through the programmes 
of Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, Swashakti project, Swayamsidha 
Project, Swawlamban programme and Support to Training & 
Employment Programme (STEP). 
21 

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2005] 
■ Periodic review of laws with a view to remove provisions which may 
be discriminatory to women and to enhance punishments for crimes 
against women as well as enactment of new laws. 
■ Sensitisation of judiciary and police and civil administration on gender 
issues. 
■ Follow up of reports of cases of atrocities against women received 
from various sources, including NCW, with concerned 
authorities in the Central and the State Governments. 
'Public order' and 'police' are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution of India and as such registration, investigation, detection and 
prevention of crime are primarily the responsibility of the State Governments. 
However, the Government of India has been advising the State Governments, from 
time to time, to give more focused attention to improving the administration of 
criminal justice system and to take such measures as are necessary for the 
prevention of crime against women and other vulnerable sections of society. The 
measures suggested include: 
■ Sensitizing of police officials charged with the responsibility of 
protecting the women; 
■ Vigorously enforce the existing legislation relating to dowry violence. 
■ Set up women police cells in police stations and exclusive women 
police stations. 
■ Provide institutional support to the victims of violence. 
■ Provide couseling to victims of rape. 
■ Ensure wider recruitment of women police officers. 
■ Train police personnel in special laws dealing with atrocities against 
women. 
■ Setting up of Fast Track Courts. 
■ Setting up of Family Courts. 
■ Appointment of Dowry Prohibition Officers and notification 
"of Rules under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 by the State 
Governments.

Compulsory education for children 
† *370. DR. FAGUNI RAM: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is mandatory to provide compulsory education to the children 
in the age group of 6 to 14 years; and 
(b) the provisions made by Government to provide compulsory education to 
the children who are staying away from th eir parents/ guardians alongwith the 
number of such children in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIARJUN SINGH): (a) and (b) Provision of Free and Compulsory Education to 
children of 6—14 years is a Constitutional mandate. Under the Centrally sponsored 
scheme of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Central Government gives assistance to States, 
inter alia, for provision of free textbooks to all girls and SC/ST boys. Under this 
scheme, Education Guarantee Scheme and Alternative and Innovative Education 
Centres are also run for children in remote areas and those who cannot attend 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
34 

[22 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
regular schools, and certain other ince ntives like free uniform to girls can 
also be provided in educationally backward blocks. In addition, Central 
Assistance is also being given for provision of cooked Midday-Meals to 
children at the Primary stage, and fo r running residential schools for girls 
from weaker sections in selected educationally backward blocks. Taken 
together, these measures substantially address the problem of participation of 
all children in elementary education including those who may be staying away 
from their parents/ guardians. Data is collected on out-of-school children but 
"Children staying away from their parents/guardians" is not a recognized 
category for which data is collected.

Observation of UNESCO on World Heritage Sites 
2666. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the Minister of CULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that any delegation of UNESCO has recently 
visited to examine the three World Heritage Sites in Agra-Taj, Agra Fort and 
Fatehpur Sikri, Hampi in Karnataka and Bodhgaya in Bihar; 
(b) if so, their observations on these World Heritage Sites and 
Government's raction thereto; 
 
(c) whether Government have requested to add more sites/places in the 
list of World Heritage Sites; and 
(d) if so the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY): (a) and 
(b) The UNESCO/ICOMOS Missions recently visited the Mahabodhi Temple, 
Bodhgaya (Bihar) in April, 2005 and Hampi (Karnataka) in August, 2005 in 
connection with finalization of Site Management Plans. 
In case of Bodhgaya, the Mission has recommended that the work on 
Site Management Plan may be suspended until such time all necessary 
conditions for implementation of the sa me are in place; namely appropriate 
legal framework, controls in the buffe r zone, management mechanism, etc. 
The Mission also recommended to expl ore the possibility of a long term 
extension of the Mahabodhi Temple Complex inscription to include the 
cultural landscape identified with Lord Buddha and other properties 
associated with the life of Buddha in India like, for example, Sarnath. 
Mahabodhi Temple at Bodhgaya is not a centrally protected monument. It is 
managed and 
61 

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2005] 
maintained by the Government of Bihar through the Bodhgaya Temple 
Management Committee constituted under Bodhgaya Temple Act, 1949. 
In case of Hampi, discussions were held with officials of Government 
of Karnataka, ASI and other stakeholders and it was decided to formulate an 
operational management plan to strengthen the functioning of the Hampi World 
Heritage Area Management Authority at Hampi. The suggestion of UNESCO 
mission to establish a technical unit is receiving the attention of the 
Government of Karnataka. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The Government of India has nominated Majuli 
Island in Assam for consideration of inclusion in the World Heritage List in 
the year 2006. Besides, the Government would also be resubmitting the 
nomination dossiers of Red Fort.

(c) The Government has initiated action in the following areas to 
ensure empowerment of women:— 
• enactment of legislations to protect women against domestic

• setting up of helplines for women in distress. 
• support services to victims of violence through schemes such as

programmes of Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, Swashakti Project, 
Swayamisdha Project, Swawlamban Programme and Support to 
Training & Employment Programme (STEP). 
• periodic review of laws with a view to remove provisions which may 
be discriminatory to women and to enhance punishments for crimes 
against women as well as enactment of new laws. 
• sensitization of judiciary and police and civil administration on 
gender issues. 
• follow up of reports of cases of atrocities against women r eceived 
from various sources, including NCW, with concerned authorities in 
the Central and the State Governments.

'Public order' and 'Police' are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India and as such registration, investigation, detection and 
prevention of crime are primarily the responsibility of the State Governments. 
However, the Government of India has been advising the State Governments, from 
time to time, to give more focused attention to improving the administration of criminal 
justice system and to take such measures as are necessary for the prevention of crime 
against women and other vulnerable sections of society. The measures suggested 
include: 
• sensitizing of police officials charged with the responsibility of protecting 
the women; 
• viogorously enforce the existing legislation relating to dowry violence"; 
• set up women police cells in police stations and exclusive women police 
stations; 
• provide institutional support to the victims of violence; 
• provide counseling to victims of rape; 
• take measures to eliminate trafficking in women. States have also been 
advised to constitute State Advisory Committees to advise on trafficking 
matters; 
• ensure wider recruitment of women police officers; and 
• train police personnel in special laws dealing with atrocities against 
women. 
• Setting up of Fast Track courts. 
• Setting up of Family Courts. 
• Appointment of Dowry Prohibition Officers and notification of rules under 
the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 by the State Governments.

SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN:

[22 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA

BHARDWAJ): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) In paragraphs 53 and 54 of the judgement of the Supreme 
Court in the matter of Salem Bar Association Vs Union of India has 
observed as under: 
"53. The Committee has also suggested that: 
Further, there must be 'judicial im pact assessment' as done in the 
United States, whenever any legislation is introduced either in Parliament or in 
the State Legislatures. The financial memorandum attached to each Bill must 
estimate not only the budgetary requirement of other staff but also the 
budgetary requirement for meeting the expenses of the additional cases that 
may arise out of the new Bill when it is passed by the legislature. The said 
budget must mention the number of ci vil and criminal cases likely to be 
generated by the new Act, how many courts are necessary, how many Judges 
and staff are necessary and what is the infrastructure necessary. So far in the 
last fifty years such a judicial impact assessment has never been made by any 
legislature or by Parliament in our country. 
54. Having regard to the constitutional obligation to provide fair, quick 
and speedy justice, we direct the Central Government to examine the 
aforesaid suggestions and submit a report in this Court within four months". 
(c) Invariably, whenever a Bill if enacted and brought into 
operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of 
India, a  Financial Memorandum is appended to such Bill to indicate 
the expenditure, recurring and non-recurring. The provisions of the Bill

tribals from their traditional habitats; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government propose to make certain changes in the tribal 
policy/law with a view to prevent eviction of tribal people; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether the Ministry of Environment and Forests has been 
consulted in this regard; and 
(0 if so, their response thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS (SHRI P.R. KYNDIAH): (a) 
and (b) As a result of inadequate recognition of the rights of forest dwelling 
Scheduled Tribes over land, where they had been living for generations, the 
threat of eviction persists. However, in order to safeguard the interests of the 
tribals and forest dwellers whose disputed claims are yet to be settled, the 
Ministry of Environment & Forests has, without prejudice to Supreme Court's 
Order, and as an interim measure,  advise the State Governments on 
21.12.2004 and 12.5.2005 that they should not resort to the eviction of tribal 
people and forest dwellers other than ineligible encroachers, till the complete 
survey is done for the recognition of su ch people and their rights as per the 
guidelines for the settlement of such claims. The State/UT Governments have 
been advised to exclude such tribaIs/forest dwellers, other than ineligible 
encroachers, from the eviction drives . Simultaneously, it has also been 
clarified that this interim measure do es not stop the State/UT Governments 
from evicting the ineligible encroachers from forest lands. 
(c) to (f) Yes, Sir. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has been mandated to 
formulate a comprehensive Central legislation to redress the historical injustice 
done to forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes by providing for clear assertion of 
their legal rights on land and other traditional forest rights.

Ministries, including the Ministry of Environment & Forests. 
The Bill was posted on the website of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs 
seeking comments/suggestions from th e members of the public, the social 
activists, academicians, anthropologists, the experts working for the cause of 
environmental protection and welfare of tribal people and other stakeholders 
on the proposed legislation till 10.7.2005. The Ministry has received 
comments/suggestions from a large number of individuals/organizations. The 
proposed Bill is still a tentative draft Bill and to be finalised as per the 
established procedure taking view s and comments received from the 
stakeholders into consideration.

Compensation for land acquisition 
2788. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the policy, procedure and practice being adopted for making payment of 
compensation to the land owners whose land is acquired; 
(b) whether compensation is paid through Addl. District Judge or Land 
Acquisition Collector directly; 
200 

[22 August, 2005] RAJYASABHA 
(c) the number of appealable and non-appealable cases in which 
payment of compensation has been made directly by the land Acquisition 
Collector, South Delhi to land owners du ring the last three years, year-wise; 
and 
(d)whether any payment in respect of  non-appealable case has been 
sent to Addl. District Judge for disbursement alongwith names and award 
numbers? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM 
NABI AZAD): (a) Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi 
(GNCTD) have reported that as per policy the payment of original 
compensation to the land owners whose land is acquired is made by the Land 
Acquisition Collector (LAC) Office after receipt of payment from 
Requisitioning Department. The landowners are required to submit surety 
bond, affidavit and ownership proof of the property. 
(b) Original compensation is paid by LAC directly. In case of any 
dispute regarding claimant, compensation amount is sent to Additional 
District Judge Court under section 30,31 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894. 
Earlier the enhanced compensation both appealable as well as nonappealable 
were sent to the Court of Additional District Judge (ADJ) for disbursement. 
As per revised procedure introduced in 2005 payment of non-appealable 
enhanced compensation is made directly by the LAC to the land owners 
subject to furnishing of relevant documents. 
(c) and (d) 2003   - Nil 
 
2004 - Nil 
2005 - Payment is 8 cases of non appealable 
enhanced compensation have been 
directly made by LAC (South). 
All payments in cases of non-app ealable enhanced compensation prior 
to adoption of revised procedure have been sent to ADJ for disbursement 
alongwith the names and award numbers.

SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA (Tamil Nadu): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, at the 
outset, I welcome the Railways (Amendment) Bill, 2004. However, I have got 
some suggestions on this Bill. The Constitution of a Railway Development 
Authority is a welcome step. 
While utilising the vacant land of the Railways, the rich people should not be 
permitted to monopolise it. There must be some eligibility criteria such as the 
unemployed youth, women, widows, handicapped persons, socially and 
economically backward people, poor people should be given priority. 
It has been mentioned in the Bill that the Member Engineering shall be the 
Chairman, ex-officio of the Authority and the rest of the members 
257 

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2005] 
are to be appointed by the Central Government. I am also having some 
suggestions on this clause. The vast lands were once acquired by the 
State Government from the public for the development of the Railways. 
In this case, the State Government should be given some priority for 
appointing officials. Hence there must be a scope for having one State 
nominee representing each State in the said Authority. Further, the 
State nominee should be consulted and on his concurrence only the 
lease should be finalised. While leasing the land in a particular State, 
the resident of that State, who is the son of the soil, should be given 
preference. If the lease amount is beyond Rs. 50 lakhs, then it should 
be published in the newspapers so that the general public could know 
about it and they also could make us e of this opportunity. Also, the 
sale price of articles sold on the leased land of the Railways shall be 
controlled by the Authority. Otherwise, they will fix their own price, and 
there will be no control over them. The purpose of the Railway Land 
Development Authority is to work for the welfare of the public. So, the 
Authority should control the prices. 
Then, the land leased shall not be used for black marketing or 
hoarding. To ensure this, the Authority should control the land so leased. 
One more suggestion is that if any lease is granted beyond five 
years period, then, it should have th e approval of the Railway Board. 
This way the Railway Board has contro l over the Authority. And, if any 
permanent structure is permitted to be constructed on the leased land, 
then, the lessee can have no claim over the structure after the lease 
period. So, clear rules and regulations should be framed for this 
Authority. 
Then, Sir, I have been stressing on this point, again and again, that 
whenever we have some development work, priority should be given 
to women as well as socially backward people. 
With these few words, I welcome the Amendment Bill. 
SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN (Kerala): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, 
I thank you for giving me this opportunity to speak a few words on this 
Bill. Though it is a simple Bill and seems to be harmless, I would like to 
support this Bill with serious appr ehensions. Therefore, I am seeking 
certain clarifications from the hon. Minister. 
258 

 [22 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
When I say I support this Bill with some apprehension, I would like 
to know what the real purpose of this Bill is. Is the real purpose of the 
Bill just to have commercial utilisation of the surplus land adjoining the 
railway track or is it that it would result in serious social implications? 
Sir, my first point is regarding lakhs and lakhs of poor people who 
are landless and poor people staying on the lands adjacent to the 
railway tracks. What would be the fate of these poor people once this 
Bill is passed? As far as this Bill is concerned, the commercial utilisation 
of the land, which is adjoining the railway tracks, will be used for getting 
revenue profit or revenue income. If that be the case, definitely, this 
Bill will result in mass evacuation of the poor people. That is my first 
apprehension. I need not mention here that the railway network in India 
is the largest network in terms of t he infrastructure facilities available 
with it, and I also take this opportunity to appreciate the hon. Minister's 
earnest efforts in bringing up the Indian Railways as the best railway 
system in the world. For this, I would congratulate him and appreciate 
the hard and earnest steps being taken by the hon. Minister on this. At 
the same time, I would like to know from the hon. Minister whether this 
Bill, once it is passed by this hon. House, would create mass 
evacuation of the poor, landless people who are staying on the adjacent 
sides of the railway tracks. This is what my fear is. 
Having said this, I can't understand how this Bill has come before 
the House, if the purpose is to hav e commercial utilisation of the land. 
If that is the mere purpose which is sought to be achieved by way of 
this Bill, then, a mere amendment of Section 11 of the Railways Act 
would have sufficed. What is the meaning of this Railway Land 
Development Authority? Clause 4 (B) says, "There will be a Chairman, 
Vice-chairman and not more than four members including experts from 
outside the railway administration." And, as per clause 4 (A) of the Bill, 
it says that the Railway Land Development Authority will be constituted 
to exercise such powers. Now what are those powers? As such, there 
are going to be no independent powers. It is very interesting to see 
here who the Chairman is going to be. Member Engineering is going 
to be the ex officio Chairman. If that is the case, then the Railway 
Ministry is going to be the real authority. So, what is the intention behind 
the formation of such a regulatory authority, the Rail Land Development 
Authority? 
259 

RAJYA SABHA [22 August, 2005] 
Now, Section 4D says, "The authority shall discharge such 
functions and exercise such powers of the Central Government or a 
railway administration in relation to the development of railway land 
and as are specifically assigned to it by the Central Government". So, 
the authority will discharg e those functions that are assigned to it by 
the Central Government or the ra ilway administration, which means 
that this authority will only be an implementing agency. Does this 
authority have the power to determine whether a particular plot of land 
can be used commercially? No. There is no such power. That is why I 
am suggesting that a mere amendment in Section 11 is sufficient for 
this purpose. Then, what is the doubt? Now, you have the Chairman, 
the Vice-Chairman and the others. Just now, as Shrimati N.P. Durga 
has also mentioned that there is nobody in the authority who has got 
the expertise in the field of land management or forests or related 
fields. You have two members, namely, Member Engineering and 
Member Traffic who are being nominated in the authority. So, my 
submission is that we should make an amendment in Section 11 of the 
principal Act, after clause (d), the following words should be inserted and 
it should read as, "(da) developing any railway land for commercial use 
for which this authority is creat ed". Sir, the authority is a pucca railway 
authority, having no independent functioning and powers. Then, what is 
the meaning and what are the functions of this authority? The authority 
is there only to implement the directions or the orders of the railway 
authority. Who is the Chairman? Member Engineering is the Chairman. 
So, this authority does not have any independent power. That is why I 
have an apprehension that after the Rail Land Development Authority 
has come into existence, whenever there is a mass evacuation of 
people take place, it will, definitely, adversely affect those poor people. 
Also, this august House had passed a legislation regarding 
resettlement and rehabilitation two years back, and in that there was a 
specific provision that whenever any land was proposed to be taken 
over by the Government, the first and the foremost step to be taken 
would be rehabilitation and resettlement of the people; the 
development work would start only after that. That is the law which had 
been passed. If that is the case, will the hon. Minister, who knows the 
problems of the poor people, the common man, assure the House that, 
while acquiring land adjacent to the railway tracks for commercial use, 
those poor, landless people are properly rehabilitated and their

With these apprehensions and clarifications sought by me, I would
